headline: CrowdStrike acquires 2 AI security startups for nearly $500M
summary: The cybersecurity giant is expanding its AI security offerings with the acquisitions of Fiddler AI and Dreadnode, aiming to secure the growing use of AI agents and models.
details: Cybersecurity leader CrowdStrike is making a significant move into AI security by acquiring two companies, Fiddler AI and Dreadnode, for a combined total of nearly $500 million. This strategic expansion aims to bolster CrowdStrike's ability to monitor, test, and secure the rapidly increasing deployment of AI models and agents across various industries.

The company is reportedly paying approximately $400 million for Fiddler AI, which specializes in observability software for monitoring AI agents within enterprises. Dreadnode, acquired for about $95 million, focuses on automating security testing to detect flaws in AI models and applications before they go live.

These acquisitions come at a critical time as businesses increasingly adopt AI technologies, often outpacing their security policies and processes. The widespread experimentation with AI tools, workflow automation, and AI agents by employees creates new challenges for security teams.

CrowdStrike, a well-established player in enterprise and government cybersecurity, aims to leverage its existing market presence to capture a share of the burgeoning AI security market. Many startups are also emerging in this space, focusing on the inadequacy of traditional security software for managing AI tools.

Fiddler AI's technology will be integrated into CrowdStrike's Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, enhancing the evaluation, monitoring, and telemetry of deployed AI agents. Dreadnode's capabilities will be incorporated into the Falcon Guardian product, providing automated security testing results and policy recommendations.
Fiddler AI, founded in 2018, had previously raised around $99 million. Dreadnode, a more recent startup founded in 2023, had secured $14 million in funding.
